poly-vocabulary.why: Degree and leading coefficient are the two numbers that control a polynomial's large-scale behaviour: the degree says how many turns and roots are possible, and the leading coefficient says which way the ends go. Naming the parts precisely is what lets you predict a graph before plotting anything.
traps: Standard form means highest power first. Degree and leading coefficient are read from that order, so put it in order first.

poly-add-sub.why: Adding polynomials is just collecting like terms, because only matching powers can combine. Subtraction is the same with one extra step that causes most of the errors: the minus sign applies to every term in the bracket.
traps: ~(3x^{2} + 2x - 1) - (x^{2} - 4x + 5)~ becomes ~3x^{2} + 2x - 1 - x^{2} + 4x - 5~. All three signs flip, not just the first.

poly-multiply.why: Multiplying polynomials is the distributive law applied repeatedly: every term in one bracket meets every term in the other. The grid or area picture is worth keeping in mind, because it makes it obvious when a product has been missed.
traps: Count your products: two binomials give four, a binomial times a trinomial gives six. If you have fewer, you dropped one.
Add exponents when multiplying powers; never multiply them.

special-products.why: Three patterns appear so often they are worth recognising instantly: ~(a+b)^{2}~, ~(a-b)^{2}~ and ~(a+b)(a-b)~. Knowing them forwards speeds up expanding; knowing them backwards is what makes factoring fast.
traps: ~(x + 5)^{2}~ is **not** ~x^{2} + 25~. The middle term ~10x~ is real and forgetting it is the single most common algebra error there is.
Only the difference of squares collapses. ~x^{2} + 25~ does not factor over the integers.

poly-divide.why: Polynomial division answers 'is this a factor?' and 'what is left over?'. A remainder of zero means the divisor divides exactly, which connects division to factoring and, later, to finding roots.
traps: Keep place-holders for missing powers when dividing: write ~x^{3} + 0x^{2} - 4x + 1~ so the columns line up.
